autonomy.label: What this AI capability means
autonomy.mcpInstall.does: Once installed, the AI employee can call everything this tool server offers on its own — it won't ask you before each call.
autonomy.mcpInstall.asks: It still stops and waits for your approval in the inbox for any action the tool itself flags as needing one.
autonomy.mcpInstall.revoke: Come back here and press Remove any time — the AI employee loses access to this tool immediately.
autonomy.automation.does: When on, the AI employee plans multi-step tasks on its own and adjusts how the team works together, without you issuing each step.
autonomy.automation.asks: It still stops and waits for your approval in the inbox for any step it judges risky or outside its authority.
autonomy.automation.revoke: Turn the switch off to go back to single-step, you-approve-each-move behavior immediately — it doesn't touch work already done.
autonomy.autopilotDelegate.does: When this rule fires, the system automatically hands the task to the agent you named, using the template text you filled in.
autonomy.autopilotDelegate.asks: Anything that agent runs into that needs approval still stops in the inbox as usual — this rule doesn't skip that step.
autonomy.autopilotDelegate.revoke: Disable or delete the rule and it stops triggering this delegation.
autonomy.browserComputerUse.does: Once approved, the AI employee can directly control the screen, mouse, and keyboard in your place.
autonomy.browserComputerUse.asks: Every task that needs this capability shows up in the inbox for your approval first — approving once doesn't grant it forever.
autonomy.browserComputerUse.revoke: Remove the grant from the approval list, or decline the next request, and the AI employee can no longer touch the screen.
autonomy.calibration.does: When on, the AI employee notes how confident it is before each judgment call, then corrects that confidence against what actually happened.
autonomy.calibration.asks: This is purely an internal self-calibration step — it never makes the AI employee do anything new, and it never skips an existing approval.
autonomy.calibration.revoke: Turn the three switches back off in order and behavior returns to exactly what it is today.
autonomy.skillSynthesis.does: When on, the system writes a new skill straight into the skill library whenever it detects a repeated capability gap — without you reviewing a draft first.
autonomy.skillSynthesis.asks: Keep "preview only" on at the same time and you'll see what it plans to add before anything is actually written.
autonomy.skillSynthesis.revoke: Turn off auto-run any time — new skills then stay as drafts until you manually approve them.
autonomy.voiceSttCommand.does: Whatever command you put here runs directly on the server to transcribe your recording — it's effectively handing the system an executable script.
autonomy.voiceSttCommand.asks: The command runs exactly as written; the system does not review or sandbox it — only use commands from a source you trust.
autonomy.voiceSttCommand.revoke: Clear this field and save, and the system stops running any transcription command.
autonomy.routinesEnable.does: When on, this AI employee runs this job in the background on the schedule you set, with no manual trigger needed.
autonomy.routinesEnable.asks: Anything it hits along the way that needs approval still stops in the inbox — the routine itself never skips that step.
autonomy.routinesEnable.revoke: Turn it off to pause immediately — it won't run again even when the next scheduled time arrives.
autonomy.osNative.does: When on, the AI employee continuously senses what's running on this device and what's changing on screen, and can act on that on its own.
autonomy.osNative.asks: It only messages you proactively when it judges something needs your decision (like an anomaly) — otherwise it stays quiet.
autonomy.osNative.revoke: Turn the main switch off and the AI employee stops sensing this device immediately, back to answering only when you ask.
autonomy.skillsInstall.does: Once installed, this skill's behavior becomes part of what the AI employee can use on its own, applied automatically whenever a matching situation comes up.
autonomy.skillsInstall.asks: If the skill's content includes an action that needs approval — like file access or an outbound connection — it still stops for your decision as usual.
autonomy.skillsInstall.revoke: Uninstall it from the skill library and the AI employee loses this skill immediately, without touching work it already finished.
autonomy.expertsApply.does: Once applied, this AI team's bundled automation scripts start running, letting the AI employee act on its own from there.
autonomy.expertsApply.asks: The scripts always wait in the inbox for your approval before they're enabled — applying the pack alone doesn't start them.
autonomy.expertsApply.revoke: Remove this install and the scripts are disabled immediately — the AI employee stops acting on them.
